title: GSM9667523: PN0 mandibular molar tooth germs, Wnt1-Cre;Bmp2f/f mice, H3K4me3 (Input) 2; Mus musculus; ChIP-Seq
protocol: PN0 mandibular molar tooth germs were collected in ice-cold PBS, and each sequencing sample consisted of 10 tooth germs pooled as one biological replicate. Tissues were cross-linked with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature and quenched with glycine (125 mM final concentration). Samples were lysed in buffer containing 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 10 mM EDTA, 1% SDS, and protease inhibitor cocktail, and chromatin was sheared by sonication to an average fragment size of 200-500 bp. ChIP-seq were performed by Wuhan IGENEBOOK Biotechnology Co.,Ltd (http://www.igenebook.com) .An aliquot of chromatin was reserved as DNA input, and immunoprecipitation was performed overnight at 4°C with rabbit anti-H3K4me3 (ABCam, ab8580; 10 μg antibody per reaction). Immune complexes were captured using protein beads and washed sequentially as described (low-salt, high-salt/LiCl, and TE washes). Bound chromatin was eluted in 100 mM NaHCO₃ with 1% SDS, treated with RNase A (final concentration 8 μg/mL) at 65°C, followed by proteinase K digestion (final concentration 345 μg/mL) at 45°C. ChIP DNA was purified and used to prepare sequencing libraries using the NEXTFLEX® ChIP-Seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina® Sequencing (NOVA-5143-02, Bioo Scientific).

title: GSM9213280: ChIP_Col0; Arabidopsis thaliana; ChIP-Seq
protocol: ChIP was performed as in Wang et al. 2024 Nature Plants. Each sample used approximately 2g flash-frozen, unopened flower buds. Briefly, tissue was ground 2x for 90 sec in TissueLyser II and powder was resuspended in nuclei isolation buffer without formaldehyde. Once fully dissolved, 37% formaldehyde was added to final conc. 1%, and samples were incubated 12 min. Crosslinking was quenched with 2M glycine, and nuclei were purified and then lysed. Chromatin was sheared using a Bioruptor Plus (Diagenode) 30s on/30s off on high x 22 cycles. Sheared chromatin was incubated with 7 uL anti-FLAG antibody (1:600 dilution, Sigma) overnight at 4C. Antibody-bound chromatin was recovered using a 1:1 mix of protein A and protein G dynabeads (Invitrogen) for 2h at 4C. Beads were washed 5x before eluting bound chromatin at 65C twice. Reverse crosslinking was performed using NaCl at 65C overnight and proteins were digested using Tris pH 6.5. DNA was purified using standard phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol extraction and precipitated with sodium acetate and ethanol o/n at -20C. Precipitated DNA from ChIP was processed using the Ovation Ultra Low System V2 kit (NuGEN), and sequenced on NovaSeq X Plus.

Primers for bisulfite-converted DNA targeting the Xist-promoter proximal CpG island (chrX:103,482,090-103,482,350 mm10 from UCSC Genome Browser) were designed with MethPrimer2.0 (Li & Dahiya, 2002). PCR reactions of each sample were pooled (total volume for Xist amplicons) and cleaned with MinElute Reaction Cleanup kit (Qiagen) (2 columns per sample). Libraries were prepared with NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep kit (New England Biolabs), indexed with NEBNext Multiplex Oligos for Illumina Dual Index Set 1 (New England Biolabs) and cleaned with AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter). Concentration and size distribution of libraries were analyzed with Qubit 1x dsDNA HS (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and HS DNA D1000 Tapestation (Agilent), respectively. Libraries were sequenced 2x150bp paired-end with MiSeq, DNBSEQ G400 or Aviti sequencers.

title: GSM9374867: CD69-DP-Satb1WT-HIC-Rep2; Mus musculus; Hi-C
protocol: For ScRNA-seq, the  single-cell suspension was loaded onto a Chromium Single Cell Chip (Chromium Single Cell G Chip Kit, 10x Genomics, PN-1000120) according to the manufacturer's instructions by Guangzhou Yiyue Biotechnology Co., Ltd with the use of a Chromium Single Cell 3' GEM, Library & Gel Bead Kit v3.1 (10x Genomics, for co-encapsulation with barcoded Gel Beads at a target capture rate of about 10000 individual cells per sample. We lysed captured cells and released RNA was barcoded through reverse-transcription in individual single-cell gel beads in the emulsion (GEMS). In each droplet, complementary DNA (cDNA) was generated and amplified through reverse-transcription on a T100 PCR Thermal Cycler (Bio Rad) at 53 ℃ for 45 min, followed by 85 ℃ for 5 min and a hold at 4 ℃. Then, cDNA concentration and quality were assessed using Qubit Fluorometer (Thermo Scientific) and bioanalyzer2100 (Agilent), respectively. According to the manufacturer's introduction, scRNA-seq libraries were constructed and sequenced to a depth of 40000 reads per cell on illumina platform. For HiC-seq, one million cells were cross-linked at a final concentration of 1% formaldehyde and in room temperature for 10 min and quenched by 200 mM glycine for 5 min at room temperature. After washing with cold 1×PBS, cells were pelleted and kept at −80 ℃ until use. Subsequently, cross-linked cells were lysed to obtain nucleus, and chromatin was digested with DpnII and DdeI overnight at 37 ℃. DpnII and DdeI was inactivated at 65 ℃for 15 min, DNA fragment ends were biotinylated with biotin-dATP using Klenow large fragment (NEB, M0210V) for 90 min at 37 ℃, and the sample was diluted, and proximity ligated for 4 h at room temperature. DNA was treated with Lambda Exonuclease and Exonuclease I to remove unligated biotinylated ends. Cross-linked DNA was reversed by the addition of SDS, proteinase K, and allowed to incubate 4h at 55 ℃. DNA was purified by phenol-chloroform, followed by ethanol precipitation, and resuspended in 50 μl 1X TE. DNA was sheared to 300–500 bp by sonication subsequently, the ligated junctions were pulled down with Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 magnetic beads (Thermo Fisher Scientific, 65001). End repair, dA tailing, adapter ligation, and PCR amplification were performed on biotinylated DNA fragments bound to beads. After purification, libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform to obtain 150 bp paired-end reads. The recommended sequencing volume gene is 100G every sample. For CUT&Tag, cells were ﬁxed by 0.5% v/v formalin in PBS for 10 min and quenched using 2.5 M glycine. The ﬁxed cells were permeabilized with TritonX-100 ; Then, cells were immobilized on a polylysine-coated coverslip instead of ConA beads and treated with different primary antibodies(anti-SATB1, Abcam 109122; anti-H3K4me3, Merck millipore 04-745; anti-H3K27ac, Abcam 4729; anti-CTCF, Merck millipore 07-729; anti-RAD21, Abcam 217678) and secondary antibodies (Goat anti-Rabbit IgG). Afterward, cells were incubated with pG-Tn5 transposase(Vazyme, S614-02) for 1 h at 37℃. Sample DNA was extracted using phenol-chloroform-isoamyl alcohol and ampliﬁed by PCR. All CUT&Tag libraries were sequenced on Illumina Nova Seq 6000 platform at PE150 mode. For ATAC-seq,  approximately 5 × 10⁴ cell pellets were washed once with cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Cells were then lysed on ice for 3 minutes in 50 μL of ice-cold Lysis Buffer, which contained the following components: 10 mM Tris (pH 7.4), 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, 0.1% NP-40, 0.1% TWEEN 20, and 0.01% Digitonin. Following lysis, the cell lysate was resuspended in 1 mL of ice-cold RBS-Wash Buffer (10 mM Tris [pH 7.4], 10 mM NaCl, 3 mM MgCl₂, and 0.1% TWEEN 20) and centrifuged at 4°C and 500 ×g for 5 minutes to pellet the cellular material. The tagmentation process was performed in 1× Tagmentation Buffer (comprising 10 mM Tris [pH 7.4], 5 mM MgCl₂, 10% dimethylformamide [DMF], 33% PBS, 0.1% TWEEN 20, and 0.01% Digitonin) with the addition of 100 nM Tn5 Transposase, and the reaction was incubated at 37°C for 30 minutes. Immediately after tagmentation, free DNA fragments were purified according to the standard protocol provided with the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (QIAGEN, Cat. No. 28106, Germany). This purification step was followed by a final PCR amplification, which included 10–15 cycles using P5 and P7 primers. After post-amplification purification, the prepared libraries were subjected to sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform to generate 150-bp paired-end reads (PE150). For ACC-seq,  thymocytes were dissociated into single cells. The cell suspension was then plated onto 0.3% gelatin-coated plates and incubated for 30 minutes at 37 ℃ in RPMI-1640 medium to remove adherent cells. A total of 3×10⁵ cells were divided into three aliquots and centrifuged at 500 rcf. For the native condition, cells were resuspended, washed with ice-cold PBS, permeabilized, and tagmented using Tn5 as in the standard ATAC-seq protocol. For the 1,6-Hex+Fix and Fix-only conditions, cells were centrifuged at 500 rcf for 5 minutes and washed once with PBS. In the 1,6-Hex+Fix group, cells were resuspended in PBS containing 10% (w/v) 1,6-hexanediol (Sigma-Aldrich, 240117) for 60 seconds at room temperature. Then, 16% formaldehyde (Invitrogen, 28906) was quickly added to the PBS to a final concentration of 1%, followed by fixation at room temperature for 10 minutes. The reaction was quenched with 0.6 M glycine (final concentration) for 5 minutes at room temperature. Cells were then washed once with ice-cold PBS and centrifuged at 500 rcf for 5 minutes. Subsequent steps were performed as in the ATAC-seq protocol. For SMART-seq2, 2000 cells sorted in 2x lysis buffer(0.4% triton x-100, 4U/ul RNase inhibitor) through BD FACS.The lysate samples were vortexed and centrifuged, and placed on a preheated PCR machine for heat-treatment. Then, Smart RT buffer and RT enzyme(SuperScript II reverse transcriptase) were added, and the reverse transcription reaction was carried out according to the program. Add 2x phanta enzyme and IS PCR primers to the cDNA product obtained in the previous step and carry out the amplification reaction according to the procedure. And take out a small amount of product and run electrophoresis gel for quality control. Quantitative purification of cDNA was performed using a DNA purification kit. The purified cDNA samples were added to Tn5 buffer and Tn5 enzyme, and the reaction was interrupted according to the program. After the reaction, mix Smart Amp buffer-2, Smart Amp enzyme-2, S5XX, N7XX for library construction, purify and send for testing. title: GSM9425029: oocyte,scBS-seq,ctrl04; Mus musculus; Bisulfite-Seq
protocol: The 8-week-old mice were anesthetized by intraperitoneal injection of tribromoethanol (350 mg/kg). Following anesthesia, the mice were first perfused with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) to remove blood and interstitial fluids from the tissues. For mice designated for dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) DNA/RNA extraction, the mice were then rapidly decapitated. Ovulation during natural estrus is commonly achieved induced using hCG doses ranging from 2.5 to 10 IU. To approximate the higher hCG exposure category defined in our discovery cohort (> 6,750 IU on trigger day), we administered a medium-high dose of hCG (7.5 IU) via intraperitoneal injection to female mice in natural estrus to induce ovulation without PMSG pretreatment. In the control group, females in estrus were housed individually with a sterile vasectomized male mouse. The next morning from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., mice with vaginal plugs or 14 h after hCG injection were euthanized by cervical dislocation. Cumulus-oocyte complexes (COCs) were subsequently collected from the oviductal ampullae. Denuded metaphase II (MII) oocytes were then isolated by removing the cumulus mass using a medium containing 0.5 mg/ml hyaluronidase at 37℃. For blastocyst collection, the optimal timing occurs at 3.5 dpc (embryonic day E3.5), when embryos have reached the fully-formed blastocyst stage and are typically located within the uterine lumen. A 30-gauge Hamilton blunt needle attached to a 1 mL syringe pre-loaded with warm flushing medium is carefully inserted into the uterus at a location close to the utero-tubal junction, the anatomical boundary between the oviduct and uterine horn. The plunger of the syringe is gently depressed to flush approximately 1 mL of medium through the uterine horn, expelling the embryos and uterine fluid into a clean petri dish containing PBS. After oocytes and blastocysts washed three times with 0.1% BSA/PBS, each sample  was then transferred into 0.2 ml PCR tubes containing 2 μl lysis buffer. Transcriptome libraries were prepared following the Smart-seq2 protocol.Total RNA was extracted from dDG tissue samples using the RNeasy Plus Mini Kit (Qiagen, Cat No. 74134) following the manufacturer's protocol. The quantity and quality of the extracted RNA were assessed using a Qubit 4.0 fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer, respectively. RNA integrity number (RIN) values greater than 7.0 were considered acceptable for sequencing. Sequencing libraries were constructed using the VAHTS Universal V8 RNA-seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina (Vazyme, NR605) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Library preparation was performed by scBS-seq protocol with some modifications. For bisulfite conversion, EZ DNA Methylation-Direct Kit (Zymo Research; D5020) was used. After zona pellucida removal, we collected 16 pools ( ctrl 8, hCG8) of 10 oocytes per group and 16 pools (ctrl 8, hCG8 ) of 10 blastocysts in a single 200 μl tube containing 2.5 μl of Buffer RLT (QIAGEN; 79216). Samples were stored at -80°C. After thawing, 7.5 μl of nuclease-free water and 65 μl of CT conversion reagent (EZ DNA Methylation-Direct Kit; Zymo D5020) were added and samples were incubated in a PCR machine (98°C 8 min, 65°C 180 min). DNA was purified by using MagBinding Beads (Zymo EZ Methylation Direct MagPrep Kit, Zymo, D5044). DNA bound to the MagBinding Beads was washed by M-wash buffer once, 100 μl of M-Desulphonation buffer was applied on the beads and the incubation was done at room temperature for 15 min to complete the CT-conversion. DNA on the beads was further washed twice and then eluted with the DNA strand synthesis with 1x Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 600 nM of dNTPs, 400 nM of P5-N6-oligo1(CTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTNNNNNN). DNA mixture was denatured at 65°C for 3 min and quickly chilled. Then 1 μl of Klenow Fragment (3'-5' exo-) (Enzymatics; P7010-LC-L) was added and the strand synthesis reaction was done in the PCR machine with the following program (4°C for 5 min, 4°C rising to 37°C with increasing0.1°C every 1 sec, 37°C for 30 min, 4°C pause). Then, the remained oligos and dNTPs were deactivated by Exo-CIP™ Rapid PCR Cleanup Kit (NEB, E1050S) following the manufacture's protocol. Next, dC tailing was conducted in the presence of 1 x Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 2.5 mM of dCTPs and 1U/μL of TdT enzyme. After that, the second strand synthesis was performed by tagging the P7-G6-oligo2 (AGACGTGTGCTCTTCCGATCTGGGGGGHN) in the presence of 1 × Blue buffer (Enzymatics), 600 nM of dNTPs, 400 nM of P7-G6-oligo2 and 100 units of Klenow exo- (Enzymatics) and incubated at 37 °C for 1 h, followed by Agencourt AMPure XP beads (Beckman) purification. Final libraries were generated by 18 cycles of PCR to incorporate universal primers and index primers and purified by Agencourt AMPure XP beads. The libraries were pooled, checked and sequenced with paired-end 150-bp reads on an Illumina NovaSeq6000 platform.For RRBS, each DNA sample was extracted from dDG tissue spiked with 0.5% lambda DNA (Thermo Fisher Scientific, SD0021) and digested with the methylation-insensitive restriction enzyme MspI (NEB, M7634S), followed by end-repair, A-tailing and ligation with methylated adaptors using KAPA HyperPlus Library Preparation Kit (Roche, KK8514). After adaptor ligation, the DNA was subjected to bisulfite treatment using the DNA Methylation-Lightning Kit (Zymo, Cat. No. D5031). The bisulfite-converted DNA was then amplified using KAPA HiFi Uracil + enzyme (Roche, Cat. No. KK2802). The PCR products were purified using the AMPure XP beads at a 0.8:1 ratio (Beckman) to obtain the final RRBS library.

title: GSM9735858: cPLX018 - GluR1/2+ EV miRNA, PLX5622, Preconditioned Concussion; Mus musculus; miRNA-Seq
protocol: For GluR1/2+ EVs derived from blood serum: We collected blood at 9 days post-injury by administering a lethal dose of sodium pentobarbital (250 mg/kg) and then collecting whole blood via cardiac puncture. We allowed the whole blood to coagulate in uncoated tubes at room temperature for 30-60 minutes and then centrifuged at 433 x g for 15 min at 4C to isolate clear serum. We stored the serum at -80C until processing. We isolated GluR1/2+ EVs from serum using Track Etched NanoPOre (TENPO) devices with 3-um pore-size and immunomagnetic capture. We thawed serum and pooled 1-4 mouse serum samples immediately prior to TENPO processing, excluding serum samples with visible red blood cell contamination. We labeled neuron-enriched EVs by incubating the serum with biotinylated anti-GluR1/2 antibodies. We lysed the GluR1/2+ EVs on chip using QIAzol (Qiagen) to extract the RNA content and isolated miRNAs using miRNeasy kit (Qiagen) and stored the miRNA at -80C until library preparation. For brain nuclei isolation: We administered 250 mg/kg sodium pentobarbital (i.p.) to the mice, quickly removed the brain from the skull, and collected a 1-mm ipsilateral slice of brain tissue directly below the site of injury (-1.5-2 mm from bregma), which was flash-frozen and stored at -80C until nuclei isolation. To isolate nuclei, we first homogenized tissue according to 10X Genomics Demonstrated Protocol CG000214 Rev F: Nuclei Isolation from Cell Suspensions and Tissue for Single Cell RNA Sequencing - Mouse Brain Tissue. We next removed myelin using an iodixanol gradient (Narayanan et al, 2020). Finally, we fixed nuclei using the Evercode Nuclei Fixation v3 Kit (Parse Biosciences) and stored nuclei at -80C until library preparation. For GluR1/2+ EV miRNAs: We used the QIAseq miRNA Library Kit (Qiagen) to produce the miRNA library. We sequenced the library using the NovaSeq 6000 SP Kit (Illumina; Next-Generation Sequencing Core, University of Pennsylvania). For single nucleus RNA: We prepared the library using the Evercode WT v3 Kit (Parse Biosciences), which pools and distributes all 24 samples into 8 sub-libraries. We sequenced using the NovaSeq 6000 SP Kit (Illumina) at Penn's Next Generation Sequencing Core.

protocol: FACS purified cells (0.1 million) were lysed in 1ml cold Cell Lysis Buffer (10mM Tris pH 8, 10mM NaCl, 0.2% NP-40/Igepal) for 10min on ice. Nuclei were pelleted at 4℃ and washed once with cold 1.4 × NEB buffer 3.1 (NEB Cat#B7203S). Nuclei were then re-suspended in 25ul of 1.4 × NEB buffer 3.1 and treated with 0.1% SDS for 10min at 65℃. Nuclei were then treated with 1% Triton X-100 to quench SDS for 1h at 37℃. Chromatin was digested with 30U DpnII restriction enzyme (NEB, Cat#R0543M) at 37℃ overnight with shaking (950rpm on a thermal mixer). After overnight digestion, an additional stroke of 30U DpnII was added into the system to further digest the genome for 4 hours at 37℃. After the 2nd stroke of digestion, nuclei were incubated at 65℃ for 20min to inactivate DpnII. Digested chromatin fragments were then cooled down to room temperature and blunted with dCTP, dGTP, dTTP (Diamond Cat#B110049, B110050, B110051) and Biotin-14-dATP (active motif, Catalog No: 14138) using 6.6U DNA Polymerase I, Large (Klenow) fragment (NEB, Cat#M0210). Chromatin was then ligated in-situ with 2000U T4 DNA ligase (NEB, Cat#M0202M) for 4 hours at 16℃ followed by further incubation for 2 hours at room temperature. Chromatin was then reverse-crosslinked overnight at 65℃ in the presence of 1% SDS and proteinase K (G-clone Cat#EZ0970). After reverse-crosslinking, DNase-free RNase A (Vazyme Cat#DE111-01) was added to the system for 30min at 37℃ to remove RNA. DNA was then extracted by phenol-chloroform extraction, precipitated, and dissolved in 130ul of nuclease free water. DNA was sonicated to 200-300bp fragments with a QSonica Q800R3 sonicator (40% amplitude, 15s ON and 15s OFF, 13min sonication) and purified with VAHTS DNA Clean Beads (Vazyme Cat#N411). Biotin-labeled DNA fragments was enriched by incubation with 100μl Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 beads (Thermal Fisher Scientific, Cat#65002) at room temperature for 15min. Streptavidin C1 beads were then washed twice with 1 × B&W buffer (5mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5; 0.5mM EDTA; 1M NaCl). Beads were re-suspended in 30ul of 1 × NEB Buffer2 (NEB Cat#7002S) containing 9U of T4 DNA polymerase (NEB, Cat#M0203S) and 40uM dATG/dGTP and incubated at 20℃ for 4 hours to remove unligated fragments. Beads were then washed twice with 1 × B&W buffer and subject to library construction. DNA end repair, dA-tailing and adaptor ligation were constructed on beads, using the AHTS Universal DNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina or MGI (Vazyme, Cat# ND627-01, NDM607-02) based on the manufacture's protocol. To eluted DNA from streptavidin beads, the library mixture was treated with 0.1% SDS and incubated at 98℃ for 10min. Released DNA was collected from the supernatant and purified with VAHTS DNA Clean Beads. Finally, the library was amplified for 8 cycles on a thermal cycler, using the VAHTS® HiFi Amplification Mix. PCR products were then purified with VAHTS DNA Clean Beads and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq500 or MGI DNBSEQ-T7 sequencing platform. HiC and ChIP-seq libraries were constructed using the VATHS DNA library preparation kit from Vazyme (N607) according to the manufacture's protocol.

Live hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells were isolated on the basis of propridium iodide negativity and surface protein expression, either as lineage-/cKit+ cells (LK) or lineage-/cKit+/Sca-1+ cells (LSK). Libraries were constructed following manufacturer's instructions for Chromium Single Cell 3' Library & Bead Kit  and Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression Kit (10X Genomics). 5,000 cells were loaded for each sample and samples were sequenced in a NovaSeq 6000 sequencer (Illumina).

design_description: Mice were injected intraperitoneally with 25 mg/kg of EdU (disolved in PBS containing 5% DMSO) for 5 days at 24-h intervals, and tissues were harvested 24 h after the final injection.  Dissected mouse tissue samples were snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80C. For nuclei extraction, frozen tissues were placed inside aluminum foil, and smashed into powders with a hammer on dry ice. Then, transfer the powdered tissue into 10-20 mL nuclei lysis buffer [10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 (VWR, 97062-936), 10 mM NaCl (VWR, 97062-858), 3 mM MgCl2 (VWR, 97062-848), 0.025% IGEPAL CA-630 (VWR, IC0219859650), 0.1% Tween-20 (Sigma, P9416-100ML), 1x cOmplete, EDTA-free Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (Sigma, 11873580001)], briefly vortex, and incubate for 10-15 minutes at 4C on a rotator. Extracted nuclei were then filtered through 40 m cell strainers (VWR, 470236-276).  EdU staining was performed on thawed nuclei using Click-iT Plus EdU Alexa Fluor 488 Flow Cytometry assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, 10633), and sorted for EdU positive nuclei.  Sorted nuclei were subjected to EasySci-ATAC-seq protocol (PMID: 38036784) for single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling.
